symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Number of independent main-wave records.

symbols.name: \(k\)
symbols.def: Depth index for the canonical nested-cell selector.

symbols.name: \(m_n\)
symbols.def: Number of independent fully annotated pilot records available before the main wave.

symbols.name: \(K\)
symbols.def: Known fixed number of baseline strata.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Known fixed size of the frozen policy menu; the headline multivariate design problem has \(M\ge3\), while \(M=2\) is retained only for the reduction check.

symbols.name: \(L\)
symbols.def: Known fixed number of outcome-support points.

symbols.name: \(x\)
symbols.def: Generic baseline stratum.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: Generic binary treatment level.

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: Generic policy label.

symbols.name: \(\ell\)
symbols.def: Generic outcome-support label.

symbols.name: \(p\)
symbols.def: Known vector with component \(p_x=P(X=x)\).

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: Known randomized-treatment probabilities with component \(e_{ax}=P(A=a\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: Observed pretreatment stratum with law \(p\).

symbols.name: \(A\)
symbols.def: Observed randomized treatment with conditional law \(e\).

symbols.name: \(C_Y\)
symbols.def: Known absolute bound on the outcome support.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_L\}\subset[-C_Y,C_Y]\) contains \(L\) distinct known values.

symbols.name: \(Y(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment \(a\).

symbols.name: \(Y\)
symbols.def: Outcome satisfying \(Y=Y(A)\).

symbols.name: \(\star\)
symbols.def: A fixed symbol \(\star\notin\mathcal Y\) recording that an outcome was not acquired.

symbols.name: \(q\)
symbols.def: Component \(q_{ax\ell}=P(Y=y_\ell\mid A=a,X=x)\).

symbols.name: \(P_{p,q}\)
symbols.def: For each admissible \(p\) and \(q\), \(P_{p,q}\) is any causal law for \(X,Y(0),Y(1),A,Y\) with stratum mass \(p\), treatment propensity \(e\), and conditional marginal outcome probabilities \(q\); the dependence between \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) is unrestricted.

symbols.name: \(\eta\)
symbols.def: Known lower bound for every conditional outcome-support probability.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\)
symbols.def: For each admissible \(p\), the class is constructed in \(\mathrm{def:saturated-model}\).

symbols.name: \(q^0\)
symbols.def: Fixed interior baseline array satisfying \(P_{p,q^0}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p)\).

symbols.name: \(\delta_q\)
symbols.def: \(\delta_q=\min_{a\in\{0,1\},x\in[K],\ell\in[L]}(q^0_{ax\ell}-\eta)\).

symbols.name: \(\beta(q)\)
symbols.def: Its \((a,x)\)-entry is \(\mu_{ax}(q)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}y_\ell q_{ax\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\sigma^2(q)\)
symbols.def: Its \((a,x)\)-entry is \(\sigma^2_{ax}(q)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}(y_\ell-\mu_{ax}(q))^2q_{ax\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\pi\)
symbols.def: Component \(\pi_j(x)\) is the treatment assigned by policy \(j\) in stratum \(x\).

symbols.name: \(d_x\)
symbols.def: \(d_x=(\pi_1(x)-\pi_M(x),\ldots,\pi_d(x)-\pi_M(x))^\top\).

symbols.name: \(F\)
symbols.def: \(F=[d_1\;\cdots\;d_K]\operatorname{diag}(p)\).

symbols.name: \(\tau(q)\)
symbols.def: \(\tau(q)=\mu_1(q)-\mu_0(q)\), using the treatment blocks of \(\beta(q)\).

symbols.name: \(Q\)
symbols.def: A fixed matrix satisfying \(FQ=I_d\).

symbols.name: \(N\)
symbols.def: A fixed full-column-rank matrix with image \(\ker(F)\), so \(FN=0\).

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Coordinate for treatment-effect directions that preserve every policy contrast.

symbols.name: \(A_{\mathrm{map}}\)
symbols.def: \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\).

symbols.name: \(\theta_p(q)\)
symbols.def: \(\theta_p(q)=A_{\mathrm{map}}\beta(q)=F\tau(q)\), where both \(F\) and \(A_{\mathrm{map}}\) use the stipulated stratum weights \(p\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr P_n\)
symbols.space: sub-sigma-fields of the full two-wave experiment
symbols.def: Sigma-field generated by the independent fully annotated pilot sample of size \(m_n\) and every auxiliary random variable used by the pilot-stage design selector.

symbols.name: \(R\)
symbols.def: Indicator that the realized outcome is acquired.

symbols.name: \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\)
symbols.def: \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) when \(R=1\), and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) when \(R=0\).

symbols.name: \(r\)
symbols.def: Component \(r_{ax}=P(R=1\mid X=x,A=a)\).

symbols.name: \(\rho\)
symbols.def: Known lower bound on every main-wave annotation rate.

symbols.name: \(B\)
symbols.def: Maximum expected main-wave labeled fraction.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_B\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_B=\{r\in[\rho,1]^{2K}:\sum_{x=1}^{K}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}\le B\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H\)
symbols.space: nonempty compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^d\)
symbols.def: Fixed set of local welfare-contrast states containing the origin.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Generic local policy-welfare contrast state.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E=\{s:\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}s_{ax\ell}=0\text{ for every }(a,x)\}\).

symbols.name: \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}\)
symbols.def: \((B_{\mathrm{mean}}s)_{ax}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}y_\ell s_{ax\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\)
symbols.def: \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}=A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}\).

symbols.name: \(S_0\)
symbols.def: A fixed linear map satisfying \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0=I_d\).

symbols.name: \(W\)
symbols.def: A fixed linear bijection onto the contrast-preserving tangent kernel.

symbols.name: \(v\)
symbols.def: Coordinate for every contrast-preserving cell-mean and outcome-shape tangent.

symbols.name: \(C_v\)
symbols.def: Fixed radius used before the outer iterated limit expands the nuisance fiber.

symbols.name: \(q_n(h,v)\)
symbols.def: \(q_n(h,v)=q^0+s(h,v)/\sqrt n\).

symbols.name: \(O\)
symbols.def: \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P^{r}_{p,q}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the sample space of \(O\)
symbols.def: Law of \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) induced by \(P_{p,q}\), \(R\mid(X=x,A=a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r_{ax})\), annotation ignorability, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \(g_s(O)\)
symbols.space: measurable real functions on the sample space of \(O\)
symbols.def: For \(s\in\mathcal E\), \(g_s(O)=R\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbf 1\{Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y_\ell\}s_{AX\ell}/q^0_{AX\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(J_r(s,t)\)
symbols.def: \(J_r(s,t)=\sum_{x=1}^{K}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}s_{ax\ell}t_{ax\ell}/q^0_{ax\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\Delta_n(s)\)
symbols.def: \(\Delta_n(s)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}g_s(O_i)\), formed from the main-wave records conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\).

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{rem}_{n,r}(h,v)\)
symbols.space: real-valued random functions on \(\mathcal H\times\mathbb R^{2K(L-1)-d}\)
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{rem}_{n,r}(h,v)=\log\{d(\mathbb P^r_{p,q_n(h,v)})^{\otimes n}/d(\mathbb P^r_{p,q^0})^{\otimes n}\}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Delta_n(s(h,v))+J_r(s(h,v),s(h,v))/2\), where every \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,R_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

symbols.name: \(\Sigma(r)\)
symbols.def: \(\Sigma(r)=\sum_{x=1}^{K}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)d_xd_x^\top/(e_{ax}r_{ax})\).

symbols.name: \(I_r\)
symbols.def: \(I_r=\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}/\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\}\).

symbols.name: \(T_r\)
symbols.def: \(T_r=I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T_r\)
symbols.def: For \(b\in\mathbb R^d\), \((\mathcal T_rb)_{ax\ell}=(T_rb)_{ax}q^0_{ax\ell}(y_\ell-\mu_{ax}(q^0))/\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_r\)
symbols.def: \(\Pi_rs=\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s\).

symbols.name: \(U_{n,r}\)
symbols.def: \(U_{n,r}=\Sigma(r)(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r)\), identifying the linear functional \(b\mapsto\Delta_n(\mathcal T_rb)\) with its Euclidean coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^d\).

symbols.name: \(Z\)
symbols.def: Limit observation with law \(N(h,\Sigma(r))\).

symbols.name: \(\Delta_M\)
symbols.def: Simplex of randomized terminal choices among the frozen policies.

symbols.name: \(\delta\)
symbols.def: A possibly randomized rule mapping the Gaussian policy-contrast signal to a terminal policy distribution.

symbols.name: \(\psi_n\)
symbols.space: measurable maps from pilot and main-wave observations to \(\Delta_M\)
symbols.def: A generic randomized terminal rule based on \(\mathscr P_n\) and \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).

symbols.name: \(\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\)
symbols.def: With \(h_M=0\), \(\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)=\max_{k\in[M]}h_k-h_j\).

symbols.name: \(L(r)\)
symbols.def: \(L(r)=\inf_\delta\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}E_{Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))}[\sum_{j=1}^{M}\delta_j(Z)\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)]\).

symbols.name: \(\sigma\)
symbols.def: Standard deviation in the one-dimensional two-policy Gaussian benchmark.

symbols.name: \(L_{\sigma}(\mathcal H)\)
symbols.def: When \(M=2\) and \(\mathcal H\subset\mathbb R\), \(L_{\sigma}(\mathcal H)=\inf_\delta\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}E_{Z\sim N(h,\sigma^2)}[\sum_{j=1}^{2}\delta_j(Z)\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)]\).

symbols.name: \(V^*\)
symbols.def: \(V^*=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B}L(r)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\)
symbols.def: Class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:admissible-procedures}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal A\)
symbols.def: Generic admissible procedure sequence.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal A^*\)
symbols.def: Procedure derived by \(\mathrm{thm:feasible-risk-attainment}\) from the implementation handle.

symbols.name: \(J_n(\mathcal A)\)
symbols.def: Policy label output by procedure \(\mathcal A\) after its pilot and main wave.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)=\lim_{C_v\to\infty}\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}E_{P_{p,q_n(h,v)},\mathcal A}[\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,J_n(\mathcal A))]\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A)=\lim_{C_v\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}E_{P_{p,q_n(h,v)},\mathcal A}[\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,J_n(\mathcal A))]\).

symbols.name: \(P_B\)
symbols.def: For \(z=\rho\mathbf 1+u\), \(P_B(z)=\rho\mathbf 1+\min\{1,(B-\rho)/(\sum_{x,a}p_xe_{ax}u_{ax})\}u\), with the constant convention at \(u=0\) or \(B=\rho\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\)
symbols.def: Order the \(2K\) annotation-rate coordinates as \((r_{01},r_{11},r_{02},r_{12},\ldots,r_{0K},r_{1K})\). Order child multi-indices \(b=(b_{01},b_{11},\ldots,b_{0K},b_{1K})\in\{0,1\}^{2K}\) lexicographically in that coordinate order, with \(0<1\). Set \(\mathcal D_0^\dagger=[\rho,1]^{2K}\). Given \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), index its \(2^{2K}\) closed dyadic child boxes by \(b\) and define \(\mathcal D_{k+1}^\dagger\) to be the lexicographically first child \(D_b\) satisfying \(\mathcal R_B\cap D_b\ne\varnothing\) and \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B\cap D_b}L(r)=V^*\). A point on a boundary shared by several closed children makes every child containing it separately eligible, and the same lexicographically first convention resolves that boundary tie. Only children of the already selected box \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) are eligible at depth \(k+1\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger=\mathcal R_B\cap\mathcal D_k^\dagger\). At least one eligible child exists at every depth because the closed children cover the selected parent box and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\) contains a minimizer. Thus \(\mathcal C_{k+1}^\dagger\subseteq\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), every selected cell is nonempty and closed, and \(\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_k^\dagger)\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-k}\to0\).

symbols.name: \(r^\dagger\)
symbols.def: The unique point defined by \(\{r^\dagger\}=\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). The intersection is a singleton because the cells are nested, nonempty, and closed inside the compact set \(\mathcal R_B\), while their diameters tend to zero.

symbols.name: \(a_n(L)\)
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences converging to zero
symbols.def: Law-specific rate sequence derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:coupled-measurable-attainment}\) from the certified prefix-separation profile of the exact lexicographic closed-cell sequence \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\) for \(L\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat r_n\)
symbols.def: Output of the projected nested-cell design sieve in \(\mathrm{def:implementation-handle}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\beta\)
symbols.def: Vector of fully labeled pilot cell means, clipped to the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde\beta_n\)
symbols.def: Its \((a,x)\)-entry is \(\widehat\beta_{ax}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax})/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde\theta_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\theta_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\widetilde\beta_n\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: Requested absolute width of the certified value interval.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{rep}}\)
symbols.def: The class of inputs for which \(\mathcal H\) is a nonempty compact rational polytope supplied by a finite rational-inequality encoding, \(p,e,\rho,B,\mathcal Y,q^0\) are rational or real-algebraic encoded numbers, \(\pi\) is binary encoded, and positivity, rank, compactness, and feasibility are accompanied by exact certificates.

symbols.name: \(\zeta_{\mathrm{tail}}\)
symbols.def: Positive error budget for Gaussian tail truncation.

symbols.name: \(\zeta_{\mathrm{quad}}\)
symbols.def: Positive error budget for adaptive quadrature.

symbols.name: \(\zeta_{\mathrm{round}}\)
symbols.def: Positive error budget for outward-rounding accumulation.

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{GRect}\)
symbols.space: algorithms on algebraic Gaussian parameters and rational rectangles
symbols.def: A terminating outward-rounded primitive that Cholesky-conditions a positive-definite algebraic Gaussian law, truncates one-dimensional tails at error \(\zeta_{\mathrm{tail}}\), adaptively subdivides the resulting compact iterated integral using certified derivative bounds until quadrature width is at most \(\zeta_{\mathrm{quad}}\), and accumulates interval arithmetic with outward-rounding width at most \(\zeta_{\mathrm{round}}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf C_\varepsilon\)
symbols.space: intervals, feasible designs, rules, and design-cell covers
symbols.def: Output of the represented state-net, \(\operatorname{GRect}\), projected-design-grid, and rational primal--dual certification construction at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).

symbols.name: \(\omega\)
symbols.def: An admissible tuple varying only the stratum masses, tied interior baseline outcome laws, and annotation budget, while holding \(K\), \(M\), \(e\), \(\rho\), \(\pi\), \(\mathcal Y\), \(\eta\), and \(\mathcal H\) fixed at their \(\omega_0\) values.

symbols.name: \(p^\omega\)
symbols.def: The stratum-mass coordinate of \(\omega\).

symbols.name: \(F^\omega\)
symbols.def: \(F^\omega=[d_1\;\cdots\;d_4]\operatorname{diag}(p^\omega)\).

symbols.name: \(\theta_{p^\omega}(q)\)
symbols.def: \(\theta_{p^\omega}(q)=F^\omega\tau(q)\).

symbols.name: \(q^{0,\omega}\)
symbols.def: The baseline-law coordinate of \(\omega\), required by admissibility to satisfy \(P_{p^\omega,q^{0,\omega}}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p^\omega)\) and \(\theta_{p^\omega}(q^{0,\omega})=0\).

symbols.name: \(B^\omega\)
symbols.def: The annotation-budget coordinate of \(\omega\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_B(\omega)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_B(\omega)=\{r\in[\rho,1]^{2K}:\sum_{x=1}^{K}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_x^\omega e_{ax}r_{ax}\le B^\omega\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Sigma_\omega(r)\)
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_\omega(r)=\sum_{x=1}^{4}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_x^\omega\sigma^2_{ax}(q^{0,\omega})d_xd_x^\top/(e_{ax}r_{ax})\), using the \(p^\omega\)-indexed law and welfare loadings.

symbols.name: \(L_\omega(r)\)
symbols.def: \(L_\omega(r)=\inf_\delta\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}E_{Z\sim N(h,\Sigma_\omega(r))}[\sum_{j=1}^{3}\delta_j(Z)\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)]\).

symbols.name: \(G_\omega(r)\)
symbols.def: \(G_\omega(r)=\max\{(\Sigma_\omega(r))_{11},(\Sigma_\omega(r))_{22},(\Sigma_\omega(r))_{11}+(\Sigma_\omega(r))_{22}-2(\Sigma_\omega(r))_{12}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G(\omega)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G(\omega)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in\mathcal R_B(\omega)}G_\omega(r)\).

symbols.name: \(P_\omega\)
symbols.def: For \(z=\rho\mathbf 1+w\), \(P_\omega(z)=\rho\mathbf 1+\min\{1,(B^\omega-\rho)/(\sum_{x,a}p_x^\omega e_{ax}w_{ax})\}w\), with the constant convention when \(w=0\) or \(B^\omega=\rho\).

symbols.name: \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega)\)
symbols.def: \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega)=P_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0)\). At \(\omega_0\), \(\sum_{x=1}^{4}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_xe_{ax}r^0_{\mathrm{alt},ax}=0.53724<0.55=B\), leaving budget slack \(0.01276\). Thus \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\) is already feasible, its projection equals itself, and \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0)=r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\) is the relative open set of admissible \(\omega\) satisfying \(\max_x|p_x^\omega-p_x^{\omega_0}|<10^{-6}\), \(\max_{a,x}|\sqrt{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^{0,\omega})}-1/2|<10^{-6}\), and \(|B^\omega-11/20|<10^{-6}\).

symbols.name: \(s_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.def: Dimension of the continuously parameterized action in the Higbee comparator class.

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.space: nonempty compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^{s_{\mathrm H}}\)
symbols.def: Continuously parameterized terminal-action set in the Higbee comparator class.

symbols.name: \(\gamma\)
symbols.def: Generic continuously parameterized terminal action in the Higbee comparator class.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.space: relative open neighborhoods of \(0\) in \(\mathcal H\)
symbols.def: A relative open neighborhood of the tied local state used to state the maintained smooth-optimum conditions.

symbols.name: \(W_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.space: real-valued functions on \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\times\Gamma_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.def: Population welfare criterion for a continuously parameterized policy action in the Higbee comparator class.

symbols.name: \(c_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.def: Uniform local curvature lower bound in the Higbee comparator class.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.def: The class of two-wave policy-design problems with terminal action \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm H}\), local state \(h\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\), and criterion \(W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\) such that \(W_{\mathrm H}\) is twice continuously differentiable in \(\gamma\) on a relative neighborhood of its optimizer graph, \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm H}}W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\) is a singleton contained in \(\operatorname{relint}(\Gamma_{\mathrm H})\) for every \(h\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\), and \(-\nabla_{\gamma}^2W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\succeq c_{\mathrm H}I_{s_{\mathrm H}}\) on that neighborhood.

symbols.name: \(\iota_{\mathrm H}\)
symbols.def: A generic injective map used to test whether a smooth-policy comparator preserves all three labeled terminal choices.

assumptions.condition: For every main-wave record, \(R_i\perp Y_i\mid(X_i,A_i,\mathscr P_n)\).

standard.name: Outcome-annotation ignorability imposed by randomized acquisition
Uniform interior-point positivity for a finite multinomial model
Strict interior localization in a finite multinomial model

novel.justification: Schedules such as \(m_n=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\) use a visibly small pilot share while still allowing every stratum--treatment cell to receive an increasing number of validation outcomes in fixed finite-stratum studies.

assumptions.condition: Every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) has a main-wave rate converging locally uniformly in probability to one deterministic \(r\in\mathcal R_B\).

novel.justification: Prospective validation protocols commonly require investigators to freeze a stable acquisition rule after a pilot; deterministic limiting rates formalize that precommitment while allowing finite-sample pilot adaptation.

definitions.name: Full contrast-and-shape local fiber
definitions.construction: For every fixed \(C_v<\infty\) and every \(n\) satisfying \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty/\sqrt n<\delta_q\), the local fiber of causal laws is \(\{P_{p,q_n(h,v)}:h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\), where \(s(h,v)=S_0h+Wv\) and \(q_n(h,v)=q^0+s(h,v)/\sqrt n\).

definitions.name: Correlated finite-policy Gaussian minimax game
definitions.construction: For each \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), observe \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\), choose \(\delta(Z)\in\Delta_M\), incur \(\sum_{j=1}^{M}\delta_j(Z)\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\), and define its value as \(L(r)\).

definitions.name: Deterministic-limit pilot annotation procedures
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}=\{(\mathcal A_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathcal A_n\text{ uses an independent fully labeled pilot of size }m_n,\text{ selects a measurable rate in }\mathcal R_B,\text{ labels main-wave outcomes independently by that rate, and satisfies }\mathrm{ass:pilot-vanishes},\mathrm{ass:deterministic-rate-limit}\}\).

definitions.name: Projected nested-cell and Gaussian-grid implementation handle
definitions.construction: Use \(P_B\) to generate feasible nets and use exactly the coordinate order, lexicographic child order, parent-only recursion, and closed-boundary convention fixed by \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). At depth \(k+1\), evaluate the uniform approximation test only on the nonempty feasible parts of the closed dyadic children of the unique ambient box selected at depth \(k\), retain every such child whose approximated cell value is within the prescribed vanishing tolerance of the approximated minimum over those siblings, and select the lexicographically first retained child. If a boundary point belongs to several retained closed children, treat all of them as eligible and apply that same lexicographic rule; never compare or select an unrelated cell. The empirical feasible cells are therefore a nested sequence of nonempty closed cells, because the sibling attaining the finite approximated minimum is always retained, and their ambient dyadic diameters tend to zero. Couple the resulting singleton-targeted \(\widehat r_n\) to \(\widetilde\theta_n\) and to a rectangle-constant Gaussian minimax rule whose state, observation, and integration meshes refine slowly enough for the conditional normal-approximation error to vanish.

definitions.name: Finite-grid certification construction
definitions.construction: For an input in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{rep}}\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), enumerate rational state nets from the finite rational-inequality encoding of \(\mathcal H\), project rational full-box design nets through \(P_B\), truncate and tile the Gaussian observation space by rational rectangles, call \(\operatorname{GRect}\) with explicit tolerances \(\zeta_{\mathrm{tail}}\), \(\zeta_{\mathrm{quad}}\), and \(\zeta_{\mathrm{round}}\) for every rectangle probability, solve the finite games with rational primal and dual certificates, and refine the state, design, observation, tail, integration, rounding, and optimization errors until their proved sum is at most \(\varepsilon\).

definitions.name: Internal covariance-geometry probe at the rational witness
definitions.construction: Coordinate specialization gives \(\mathcal R_B(\omega_0)=\mathcal R_B\) and \(L_{\omega_0}(r)=L(r)\). The internally chosen probe \(G_{\omega_0}\) records only the largest of the three pairwise marginal contrast variances. Form its optimizer set \(\mathcal G(\omega_0)\) and compare that set with the explicitly projected feasible design \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0)\) under the full Gaussian minimax-regret functional.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(C_v<\infty\), compactness and linearity give \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty<\infty\). Because \(\delta_q>0\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty/\sqrt n<\delta_q\), so every positive or negative coordinate tilt obeys \(q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)\ge q^0_{ax\ell}-|s(h,v)_{ax\ell}|/\sqrt n>\eta\). Uniformly on that domain, \(q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K}\), \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), and \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\). Moreover, for every bounded \(u\), some bounded nuisance coordinate \(v\) satisfies \(\sqrt n\{\tau(q_n(h,v))-\tau(q^0)\}=Qh+Nu\), while the remaining coordinates range over every common-arm-mean and zero-mean outcome-shape direction.
statements.justification: This theorem verifies that the entire \(Qh+Nu\) treatment-effect fiber and every remaining shape nuisance form a legal local submodel rather than an assumed least-favorable family.
statements.gap: Hirano and Porter localize regular models but do not construct the saturated finite-support fiber under design-dependent annotation.
statements.consumer: The nuisance-uniform lower bound uses the full fiber, including every treatment-effect and outcome-shape tangent that leaves policy contrasts unchanged.

statements.statement: At \(q^0\), the residual mean tilt in each \((a,x)\) cell is Fisher-orthogonal to every zero-mean shape tangent, the efficient cell-mean information under design \(r\) is \(I_r\), and the least-favorable lift \(T_r\) satisfies \(A_{\mathrm{map}}T_r=I_d\) and \(T_r^\top I_rT_r=\Sigma(r)^{-1}\).
statements.justification: The identities expose the exact covariance of the efficient policy-contrast signal after selective annotation.
statements.gap: Levis et al. give general observed-data influence-function projection, but not this full saturated tangent decomposition or overlapping-policy covariance identity.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the least-favorable slice and the covariance input for both the Gaussian game and the AIPW estimator.

statements.statement: Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), \(C_v<\infty\), and \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose pilot-measurable main-wave rate \(\widehat r_n\) converges locally uniformly in probability to \(r\). The strict slack \(\delta_q>0\) implies that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every positive or negative tilt on \(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) lies in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), every fixed finite collection of points in that domain obeys the observed-data expansion \[\log\frac{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)})^{\otimes n}}{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0})^{\otimes n}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\Delta_n(s(h,v))-\tfrac12J_{\widehat r_n}(s(h,v),s(h,v))+\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v),\] where \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}|\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v)|=o_{\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}}(1)\). Under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}\), the conditional finite-coordinate law of \(\Delta_n\) converges to a centered Gaussian process with covariance \(J_r\), uniformly on that compact domain. The map \(\Pi_rs=\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s\) is the \(J_r\)-orthogonal contrast projection, and under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)}\), \(U_{n,r}\Rightarrow N(h,\Sigma(r))\) uniformly on the same domain. The likelihood contribution from \(\mathscr P_n\), whose fully labeled pilot records satisfy \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\), is asymptotically negligible because \(m_n/n\to0\). Consequently, for every finite prior on \(\mathcal H\), the infimum over all \(\psi_n\) of the prior regret along the least-favorable submodels \(q^0+\mathcal T_rh/\sqrt n\), which also remain in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for both signs and all sufficiently large \(n\) by the same slack argument, converges to the Bayes regret in \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\); this finite-prior risk-transfer conclusion, rather than total-variation convergence of experiments, is the conclusion used downstream.
statements.justification: The explicit conditional LAN expansion and finite-prior transfer identify exactly what survives a discontinuous pilot design and the complete contrast-preserving nuisance fiber.
statements.gap: Hirano and Porter provide fixed-experiment scalar treatment-rule transfer, while Cook et al. provide stabilized adaptive AIPW Gaussianity; neither conditions on a pilot sigma-field to prove a design-indexed finite-coordinate LAN expansion and least-favorable finite-prior transfer over all outcome-shape tangents.
statements.consumer: It licenses lower-risk transfer for any admissible prospective annotation procedure and prevents a restricted outcome family from determining the design.

statements.statement: For every \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), the full-fiber Gaussian minimax regret equals \(L(r)\); the infimum over \(\delta\) is attained, \(L\) is continuous on \(\mathcal R_B\), and \(V^*=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B}L(r)\) is attained. The value also equals the supremum of finite-prior Bayes values over \(\mathcal H\).
statements.justification: This identifies the design objective and establishes that both the terminal rule and annotation optimum exist.
statements.gap: Masten and Kato analyze many-action games for treatment arms; the theorem concerns correlated overlapping policy values whose covariance is chosen through selective outcome observation.
statements.consumer: Prospective validators obtain a well-defined population target \(V^*\) instead of a collection of unrelated contrast variances.

statements.statement: For the theorem-level comparison, \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\) is the class of two-wave policy-design problems with a continuously parameterized action \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm H}\), local state \(h\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\), and population welfare \(W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\) satisfying the following maintained conditions: \(W_{\mathrm H}\) is twice continuously differentiable in \(\gamma\) on a relative neighborhood of its optimizer graph; for every \(h\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\), \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm H}}W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\) is a singleton in \(\operatorname{relint}(\Gamma_{\mathrm H})\); and \(-\nabla_{\gamma}^2W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)\succeq c_{\mathrm H}I_{s_{\mathrm H}}\) on that neighborhood for one \(c_{\mathrm H}>0\). At \(\omega_0\), the finite-menu choice correspondence at \(h=0\) is \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in[3]}h_j=[3]\), with \(h_3=0\), and every relative neighborhood of \(0\) in \(\mathcal H=[-1,1]^2\) contains states at which each labeled policy is uniquely welfare maximizing. If an instance of \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\) preserved the three labeled choices through an injective map \(\iota_{\mathrm H}:[3]\to\Gamma_{\mathrm H}\), in the explicit sense that \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm H}}W_{\mathrm H}(h,\gamma)=\{\iota_{\mathrm H}(j):j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{k\in[3]}h_k\}\) for every \(h\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm H}\), then at \(h=0\) its optimizer set would contain the three distinct points \(\iota_{\mathrm H}(1),\iota_{\mathrm H}(2),\iota_{\mathrm H}(3)\), directly contradicting the maintained singleton condition. Thus the rational witness is outside \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\) because its three-way tie fails uniqueness. Moreover, with \(K=4\), \(L=3\), and \(d=2\), the selectively observed model has \(2K(L-1)-d=14\) contrast-preserving nuisance coordinates, and projecting them by \(\Pi_r\) yields the design-dependent non-diagonal efficient covariance \(\Sigma(r)\). Higbee's smooth unique-optimum comparator therefore covers neither the witness's finite-menu tie geometry nor its selective-annotation nuisance step.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates both obstructions to importing smooth unique-optimum policy-design theory: a genuine three-way local tie and an observation-design-dependent nuisance projection.
statements.gap: Higbee (2026) derives two-wave policy design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum; the finite-menu tie geometry and selective-annotation nuisance experiment in this theorem lie outside those assumptions.
statements.consumer: The result tells the attainment proof exactly which smooth argmax and direct-policy-observation reductions are unavailable at the rational witness.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) has deterministic limiting rate \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), then \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge L(r)\ge V^*\). The supremum in \(\mathcal R_-\) ranges over the entire local fiber before \(C_v\to\infty\), and the claim does not require regularity or convergence of the terminal policy selector.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies the minimax converse against every measurable deterministic-limit annotation procedure.
statements.gap: Hirano and Porter do not optimize an observation design, and Nwankwo et al. optimize scalar estimation variance rather than terminal policy regret.
statements.consumer: The lower bound certifies that no alternative fixed-limit targeted follow-up scheme can uniformly beat the proposed value.

statements.statement: For every input in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{rep}}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), the construction \(\mathsf C_\varepsilon\) terminates. With explicitly chosen \(\zeta_{\mathrm{tail}},\zeta_{\mathrm{quad}},\zeta_{\mathrm{round}}>0\), every Gaussian rectangle call to \(\operatorname{GRect}\) returns an outward interval whose width is bounded by the sum of those three budgets, and the propagated certificate returns an interval containing \(V^*\) with width at most \(\varepsilon\), an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible design and Gaussian rule, and an outer finite union of design cells containing every minimizer of \(L\). No termination claim is made for an opaque real input or an oracle-free compact set.
statements.justification: The theorem places the numerical claim on an effective domain and makes every Gaussian probability and accumulated error auditable.
statements.gap: Masten proposes computational-game methods and Kato certifies a particular three-arm comparison, but neither gives a general two-sided grid theorem for a design-indexed correlated policy game.
statements.consumer: A trial designer can audit the claimed regret value, feasible rates, and all surviving optimal-design cells at a declared tolerance.

statements.statement: Using the handle in \(\mathrm{def:implementation-handle}\), construct one jointly measurable schedule of pilot tolerances, dyadic depths, state nets, Gaussian observation rectangles, and probability enclosures that uses the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, the lexicographic order on \(\{0,1\}^{2K}\), and the closed-boundary tie convention defining \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). At depth \(k+1\), the schedule must select the lexicographically first eligible child only among children of the unique ambient box selected at depth \(k\), with every child containing a shared-boundary point tested separately and no unrelated cell eligible. Prove that every fixed empirical tree prefix stabilizes to \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), hence its feasible cell stabilizes to \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), and that \(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P(a_n(L))\) locally uniformly for a deterministic law-specific rate \(a_n(L)\) derived from the certified prefix-separation profile, including disconnected, flat, tied, and dyadic-boundary minimizing sets, while the implemented rectangle rule has risk error \(o(1)\) uniformly over each bounded nuisance fiber; characterize whether any uniformly faster rate is impossible without an additional optimizer-identification modulus.
statements.justification: This is the unresolved implementation theorem: set convergence alone does not select a deterministic representative, determine its attainable rate, or control a changing discontinuous decision rule.
statements.gap: McIsaac and Cook learn a pilot-optimal allocation, Luedtke and van der Laan analyze exceptional decision laws, and Higbee assumes uniqueness and strong curvature; none supplies the required coupled selector and law-specific rate at nonunique optima.
statements.consumer: The result turns the population minimax design into a pre-specifiable two-wave protocol that remains valid when several annotation designs are exactly tied.

statements.statement: A solution of \(\mathrm{oeq:coupled-measurable-attainment}\), combined with \(\widetilde\theta_n\), yields \(\mathcal A^*\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose empirical selected ambient box at depth \(k+1\) is the lexicographically first eligible closed child of its unique depth-\(k\) selected ambient box under the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, with shared-boundary children tested separately and no unrelated cell eligible. Every fixed empirical prefix stabilizes to \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), its feasible cells stabilize to the nested population cells \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) locally uniformly in probability, where \(\{r^\dagger\}=\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). Moreover, \(\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))\) uniformly over every fixed bounded nuisance fiber, and \(\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*\). Hence the lower and upper deterministic-limit local minimax envelopes both equal \(V^*\).
statements.justification: The upper theorem matches the full-nuisance converse with an implementable pilot, joint estimator, and terminal rule.
statements.gap: Nwankwo et al. attain scalar ATE variance and Cook et al. prove scalar adaptive AIPW limits; neither couples a set-valued regret design to a multivariate discontinuous minimax rule.
statements.consumer: Independent validation of a frozen clinical-policy menu can target scarce follow-up toward the cells that minimize eventual welfare loss.

statements.statement: At \(\omega_0\), the optimizer set \(\mathcal G(\omega_0)\) of the internally chosen functional \(G_{\omega_0}\) is a singleton. For its unique element \(r\), outward-rounded certificates establish \(L_{\omega_0}(r)>0.1965\) and \(L_{\omega_0}(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0))<0.18453\). Thus minimizing the scalar maximum of the three pairwise marginal contrast variances does not determine a Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: every minimizer of \(L_{\omega_0}\) differs from that \(r\), with certified regret gap exceeding \(0.01197\) relative to the displayed feasible alternative.
statements.justification: The theorem positively identifies a feature of correlated three-policy regret geometry that the scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not preserve.
statements.gap: The inspected Gaussian treatment-choice and annotation results do not give an exact open-region example in which two designs ordered by a self-contained pairwise-variance probe are strictly reversed by the full overlapping-policy regret game.
statements.consumer: For CodiEtAl2025ClinicalRules and KimEtAl2025AzithromycinRules, prospective independent validation of the frozen ABCD azithromycin policy menu can use the internal \(G_\omega\) probe to diagnose whether a covariance summary retains enough joint information for the validation design. Neither cited paper is claimed to use or recommend \(G_\omega\).

statements.statement: For every \(\omega\in\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\), the internally defined set \(\mathcal G(\omega)\) is a singleton and, for its unique element \(r\), \(L_\omega(r)>0.1964558>0.1845960>L_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega))\), where \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega)=P_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0)\in\mathcal R_B(\omega)\).
statements.justification: An open-region theorem rules out the interpretation that separation is caused by one knife-edge rational law.
statements.gap: No inspected result establishes an open neighborhood on which an internally specified pairwise-marginal-variance probe and the full correlated welfare-regret game have strictly separated optimizer values.
statements.consumer: For CodiEtAl2025ClinicalRules and KimEtAl2025AzithromycinRules, prospective independent validation of the frozen ABCD azithromycin policy menu can use the internal \(G_\omega\) probe to diagnose whether a covariance summary retains enough joint information under small misspecification of stratum weights, budget, and arm-specific outcome variation. Neither cited paper is claimed to use or recommend \(G_\omega\).

statements.statement: If the menu is specialized to \(M=2\), then \(d=1\), \(L(r)=L_{\sqrt{\Sigma(r)}}(\mathcal H)\), and the exact scale identity is \(L_{\sigma}(\mathcal H)=\sigma L_1(\mathcal H/\sigma)\). If \(0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2\), then \(N(h,\sigma_1^2)\) Blackwell dominates \(N(h,\sigma_2^2)\) by addition of independent Gaussian noise, so \(L_{\sigma_1}(\mathcal H)\le L_{\sigma_2}(\mathcal H)\). Therefore every design minimizing the single contrast variance is regret-optimal; no converse or strict monotonicity is asserted without an additional condition on \(\mathcal H\).
statements.justification: The binary reduction is the required sanity check and isolates why three overlapping policies are the first nontrivial case.
statements.gap: Binary Gaussian treatment-choice and Neyman allocation results are known; this proposition verifies exact compatibility rather than claiming novelty.
statements.consumer: Readers can diagnose whether the new regret criterion changes design only because the action menu creates genuinely multivariate tie geometry.

sampling_model.design: Two-wave prospective outcome acquisition with a fully labeled pilot of size \(m_n\), followed by a pilot-measurable deterministic-rate main-wave design \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\).
sampling_model.units: Independent main-wave records \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) have observed law \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q}\), where \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) otherwise, with fixed finite stratum space \([K]\), binary randomized treatment, and fixed finite outcome support \(\mathcal Y\).
sampling_model.treatment: Known propensities \(e_{ax}\) satisfy conditional randomization, and the frozen policy menu \(\pi\) maps strata to binary treatments.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment propensities are strictly positive and annotation rates satisfy \(r_{ax}\ge\rho>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The vanishing pilot estimates the finitely many cell means and variances; the main wave uses the joint AIPW contrast estimator \(\widetilde\theta_n\).
sampling_model.localization: Conditional outcome arrays are \(q_n(h,v)=q^0+s(h,v)/\sqrt n\), where \(\delta_q=\min_{a,x,\ell}(q^0_{ax\ell}-\eta)>0\) ensures that every bounded positive or negative tilt lies in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). The corresponding p-indexed causal laws are \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\), with \(h\in\mathcal H\) and an iteratively expanding nuisance radius for \(v\). Conditional main-wave likelihoods are formed from \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)}\) given \(\mathscr P_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Reduces regular treatment choice with a scalar welfare contrast to a Gaussian limit experiment and transfers asymptotically minimax rules.
Establishes asymptotic minimax-regret optimality for many treatments and discusses computational-game solutions.
Derives a near-optimal two-thirds allocation for separable subgroup-specific Gaussian treatment decisions.
Derives a two-batch annotation design and AIPW estimator attaining the optimal scalar ATE asymptotic variance.
Optimizes scalar semiparametric efficiency and componentwise maximin efficiency for a fixed-dimensional parameter in two-phase studies.
Proves a semiparametrically efficient AIPW central limit theorem under adaptive treatment probabilities.
Matches exact minimax and Bayes simple-regret constants over all adaptive experiments for independent finite arms.
Obtains asymptotically Bayes-optimal two-wave design for smooth constrained policy choice under a unique, strongly concave local optimum.
Derives efficient robust estimators of smooth causal functionals under randomized double sampling.
Derives minimax-regret choice between two treatments when missing outcomes are unrestricted and treatment response is partially identified.
Solves minimax-regret treatment choice with incomplete data for finitely many treatments and shows that the two-treatment randomization pattern need not extend to three or more treatments.
Characterizes exact finite-sample minimax-regret rules for two-treatment choice with a fixed positive fraction of missing outcomes.

tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over a saturated finite-support outcome model and every contrast-preserving shape nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and seeks one measurable vanishing-pilot AIPW procedure attaining that value at tied or boundary design optima. A rational three-policy witness establishes positively that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of an internally chosen pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal annotation methods optimize scalar estimation variance, multidimensional two-phase methods optimize componentwise efficiency, and smooth policy-design theory assumes a unique curved optimum. Missing-outcome minimax-regret results instead treat exogenous incompleteness and treatment choice under partial identification; they do not choose randomized prospective annotation rates for point-identified overlapping policy loadings. None of these results combines a pilot-conditioned full-nuisance LAN transfer, correlated finite-menu regret design, nonunique deterministic selection, and certified computation.
project_justification.niche: The niche is prospective validation of a fixed overlapping causal-policy menu when investigators control scarce randomized follow-up and the operational objective is welfare loss from the final policy choice.
project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, a tie-stable pilot implementation question, and an open-region theorem showing that a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the regret-optimal design.

related_work: Hirano and Porter (2009) inform the scalar fixed-experiment Gaussian decision bridge, while Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) inform finite-action Gaussian games; none observes overlapping policy loadings through selectively annotated treatment--stratum cells. Higbee (2026) proves two-wave Bayes design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum. Theorem 4 gives the theorem-level contrast required here: the rational finite menu has a three-way tie in every local decision neighborhood and fourteen contrast-preserving selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, so Higbee's uniqueness and curvature conditions do not cover the experiment. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) supply the closest scalar annotation workflow, and the Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, supplies the nearest componentwise semiparametric two-phase criterion. Levis et al. (2024) inform observed-data influence projection, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) inform stabilized AIPW limits, and Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) identify the nonregularity of nonunique optimal decisions. Manski (2007) studies minimax-regret treatment choice when outcomes are missing for uncontrolled reasons and the response law is partially identified. Stoye (2007) extends incomplete-data choice to many treatments, and his finite-sample missing-outcome analysis studies a fixed exogenous missing fraction. Those decision problems are important antecedents but differ from prospective randomized annotation, known propensities, point-identified policy contrasts, and optimization of the acquisition design itself. Hu et al. (2024) inform regret-sensitive allocation in separable subgroup decisions. The auxiliary functional \(G_\omega\) is introduced internally only as the geometric probe in the constructive witness. Codi et al. (2025) provide the stacked rule-comparison consumer, and Kim et al. (2025) motivate independent validation of the azithromycin rules.
technical_internal_limitation: The remaining load-bearing gap is the single measurable implementation theorem in \(\mathrm{oeq:coupled-measurable-attainment}\). Under the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, lexicographic child order, parent-only recursion, and closed-boundary convention defining \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), the nested-cell prefix argument must be checked under uniform pilot and numerical errors at separated tied minima, flat minima, and a minimizer on a dyadic boundary, and then coupled to a changing Gaussian rectangle rule without claiming total-variation convergence of the discrete observed sample to a continuous Gaussian observation. Continuity alone cannot yield an objective-uniform Euclidean optimizer rate, so the claimed rate must be law-specific through certified prefix gaps, with a converse describing the absence of a faster uniform rate. Failure of fixed-prefix stabilization without adding uniqueness is an early kill condition.
honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design after a vanishing pilot. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has uniformly positive cell probabilities; binary or continuous clinical outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact validity certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, not a spatial optimizer rate. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the internal geometric probe in the witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction and the Gaussian reduction on pp. 1683--1695, together with Theorem 4.4 on pp. 1697--1699, were opened. The proof architecture transfers an optimal rule from a Gaussian limit experiment through a best regular estimator, but the published decision has one binary welfare contrast and no design-controlled missing outcome.
seed_details.question: Can the local asymptotic minimax value for choosing among overlapping policies be characterized jointly with the outcome-annotation design, uniformly over all contrast-preserving outcome-shape directions, and attained by one feasible pilot procedure?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar efficient welfare contrast in the limit experiment by the projection of the saturated cell-probability score onto the full vector of overlapping policy contrasts, with the annotation rate inside the information matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{policy annotation}+\text{minimax regret}\), \(\text{overlapping policies}+\text{Gaussian design}\), and \(\text{design-dependent covariance}+\text{policy regret}\) found scalar causal annotation, independent-arm best-arm identification, and smooth Bayes policy design, but no result with this joint object.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The kernel combines a nuisance-uniform limit experiment, a design-level minimax value, feasible attainment, and a robust strict separation; it does not claim the generality needed for a flagship result.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from Hirano and Porter because policy choice is already reduced to an efficient Gaussian statistic.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their scalar reduction holds for a fixed experiment; selective annotation makes the full contrast covariance a design variable, while the nuisance supremum includes mean-preserving shape scores and the action space has higher-order tie faces.

literature_map: Hirano and Porter (2009) provide the local scalar Gaussian treatment-rule bridge. Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) treat many-action or best-arm Gaussian decisions, while Higbee (2026) develops two-wave smooth policy design under uniqueness and strong curvature; Theorem 4 isolates the finite-menu tie geometry and selective-annotation nuisance projection outside those assumptions. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) optimize scalar causal annotation variance. The Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, optimizes scalar or componentwise semiparametric efficiency in two-phase sampling. Levis et al. (2024) and Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) provide projection and adaptive AIPW ingredients. Manski (2007), Stoye (2007) on incomplete data and many treatments, and Stoye (2007) on finite samples with missing outcomes analyze treatment choice under exogenous or uncontrolled missingness; their welfare objects are partially identified or their missing fractions are fixed, rather than chosen prospectively to learn point-identified overlapping policy loadings. Hu et al. (2024) motivate regret-sensitive allocation in a separable subgroup experiment. The witness introduces \(G_\omega\) internally as a geometric probe. Codi et al. (2025) and Kim et al. (2025) supply the frozen-rule validation consumer. The unoccupied intersection is deterministic-limit minimax annotation for correlated overlapping policy values, with a pilot-conditioned full-nuisance LAN expansion, tie-stable measurable attainment, effective certification, and a robust theorem that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the regret-optimal design.

novelty_justification: Gaussian games, three-action choice, and minimax treatment decisions with missing outcomes are not claimed as new. The new observation geometry is prospective and controlled: investigators randomize acquisition of treatment--stratum outcomes, while terminal actions are overlapping linear policy values. This yields a design-indexed non-diagonal covariance and a nuisance kernel containing every value-preserving outcome-shape direction. Relative to Higbee (2026), the theorem-level delta is exact: the rational witness has a three-way local tie and fourteen selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, violating the comparator's unique strongly concave smooth optimum conditions. Relative to Manski and Stoye, the outcomes remain point identified under known randomized treatment and annotation probabilities, and the annotation law is the design variable rather than an exogenous source of partial identification. The proposed deterministic-limit envelope is tied to an explicit conditional LAN and finite-prior transfer statement, then paired with an open measurable implementation question at nonunique and boundary optima. The rational witness adds a positive geometric theorem using only its internally defined probe: the singleton \(G_{\omega_0}\)-optimizer has regret above \(0.1965\), the displayed feasible design is below \(0.18453\), and the inequality persists on an explicit neighborhood.
